leftFaqs.question: Who offers the best IVF treatment in India?
leftFaqs.answer: Dr. Mona Dahiya can help you with your journey to parenthood with affordable price and high success rate in India.

leftFaqs.question: What is the success rate of IVF in India?
leftFaqs.answer: IVF has success rate of approximately 40%-60% in India. It may vary with the age of women and type of infertility you have. Dr Mona Dahiya has an IVF success rate of 90%+.

leftFaqs.question: What age is good for IVF?
leftFaqs.answer: Every woman is different but typically women in their 20s and early 30s will have better chances of getting pregnant. It decreases with age.

leftFaqs.question: Is IVF safe after 35?
leftFaqs.answer: Yes you can have IVF after 35 years of age. But your chances decrease as you age. There are some techniques that can increase your chance of success.

leftFaqs.question: How many IVF cycles are needed to get pregnant?
leftFaqs.answer: Everyone is different some will conceive in their first cycle and some may take longer than that. Age and Type of Infertility can effect this.

leftFaqs.question: Which month is best for IVF?
leftFaqs.answer: There is no particular month for doing IVF. You can get it done anytime of the year based on your period.

rightFaqs.question: Is IVF harmful or beneficial?
rightFaqs.answer: IVF can help you conceive a baby. However there can be side effects such as Multiple pregnancy, Ovarian hyper stimulation and stress from the treatment. All these side effects are very rare if the IVF procedure is done by an expert IVF specialist like Dr Mona Dahiya.

rightFaqs.question: How safe is IVF pregnancy in India?
rightFaqs.answer: If proper protocol is followed then IVF baby is perfectly safe. Make sure to consult the right fertility doctor like Dr Mona Dahiya.

rightFaqs.question: How can I share my medical records?
rightFaqs.answer: You can send us your report on email, whatsapp before your appointment.

rightFaqs.question: What if I don't have previous medical records?
rightFaqs.answer: We can do initial basic tests that are required to plan your treatment.

rightFaqs.question: Which documents should I carry for treatment?
rightFaqs.answer: Passport original, passport size photo and old report (if any) should be there with you.

rightFaqs.question: What is the Indian country code?
rightFaqs.answer: India's Code is: +91. To reach us internationally dial +91 92679 82924.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions: Online IVF Consultation

items.q: Is the online consultation with Dr. Mona personally?
items.a: Yes. The video call is conducted by Dr. Mona Dahiya herself after she has reviewed your records.

items.q: How long is the online consultation?
items.a: Each slot is 30 minutes, focused on history, reports and a clear next-step plan.

items.q: What do I need before the call?
items.a: Past treatment charts, recent hormone tests, ultrasound or semen reports, and a list of medicines already tried.

items.q: How do I send my medical reports?
items.a: Email them to info@drmonadahiya.com or share clearly labelled PDFs / photos on WhatsApp.

items.q: What is the fee for Indian patients?
items.a: ₹1,000 for a 30-minute consultation including a written summary after the call.

items.q: What is the fee for international patients?
items.a: US$25 covering records review, the call, and support letters when required for travel.

items.q: Will I get a written plan after the consultation?
items.a: Yes. A medical summary, digital prescription and test roadmap are shared by email or WhatsApp within about 2 hours.

items.q: Can online consultation replace an in-clinic visit?
items.a: It is ideal for second opinions and planning. Physical exams, scans and procedures still need a clinic visit.

items.q: Which platforms are used for the video call?
items.a: You receive a secure video link (commonly WhatsApp or a standard teleconsult link) after your slot is confirmed.

items.q: Can we book for both partners together?
items.a: Yes. Couples are encouraged to join the same call so the plan covers both partners.

items.q: How soon can we start treatment after the online consult?
items.a: Many couples schedule an in-clinic visit within days; timelines depend on tests and your cycle.

items.q: What is the difference between conventional IVF and ICSI?
items.a: In IVF, eggs and thousands of prepared sperm are placed together in a dish. In ICSI, an embryologist injects one selected sperm into each egg, which overcomes severe male factor and past fertilisation failure.

items.q: How long does one complete IVF cycle take?
items.a: About 12 to 14 days of stimulation from Day 2 of the period to egg retrieval. A frozen transfer adds 2 to 3 weeks of lining preparation, then a blood test 14 days later.

items.q: Is egg retrieval painful?
items.a: No. It takes 15 to 20 minutes under light IV sedation, so you sleep through it. Mild cramping afterwards settles with simple painkillers.

items.q: How many hormone injections are needed?
items.a: Small injections under the skin once a day for 8 to 11 days, using ultra-fine needles like insulin pens.

items.q: Do I need to stay in hospital?
items.a: No. Egg retrieval and embryo transfer are day-care procedures, and most women go home within 2 to 3 hours.

items.q: Which tests are needed before IVF?
items.a: AMH with an antral follicle scan, semen analysis, a uterine scan, hormone tests (TSH, prolactin) and infection screening for both partners.

items.q: When will I know if IVF worked?
items.a: A blood Beta-hCG test 14 days after transfer (or 12 to 14 days after a blastocyst transfer).

items.q: Is strict bed rest needed after embryo transfer?
items.a: No. Studies show bed rest does not improve implantation, and embryos cannot fall out. Rest 15 to 20 minutes at the clinic, then resume normal, non-strenuous activity.

items.q: How many embryos should be transferred?
items.a: Usually 1. Dr. Dahiya prefers elective single blastocyst transfer, which keeps pregnancy rates high while reducing risks of preterm birth and twins.

items.q: Are frozen transfers as effective as fresh transfers?
items.a: Yes. Vitrified embryos survive warming over 95% of the time, and frozen transfers often do as well or better because the lining is prepared without high stimulation hormones.

items.q: Does IVF increase the risk of birth defects?
items.a: The large majority of IVF babies are healthy. Some studies show a small increase in risk, mostly linked to the underlying infertility rather than IVF itself, and Dr. Dahiya discusses this at consultation.

items.q: What is OHSS and how is it prevented?
items.a: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome is an over-response to stimulation. It is prevented with antagonist protocols, careful dosing, an agonist trigger and freeze-all cycles when needed.

items.q: Can I work during IVF?
items.a: Yes. Most women keep working through stimulation and take 1 to 2 days off around egg retrieval.

items.q: What should I avoid after transfer?
items.a: Heavy lifting, intense exercise, smoking, alcohol and hot tubs until the pregnancy test.

items.q: Can I have IVF with my own eggs if my AMH is below 0.5 ng/mL?
items.a: Yes. AMH reflects egg numbers, not quality. Tailored protocols such as DuoStim or Mini IVF help many women with low AMH conceive with their own eggs.

items.q: What causes recurrent implantation failure?
items.a: Mainly chromosomal errors in embryos, hidden chronic endometritis (CD138 biopsy), uterine defects or a displaced implantation window (detected by the ERA Test).

items.q: What is the success rate of IVF with Dr. Mona Dahiya?
items.a: The clinic achieves an overall IVF success rate above 90%, peaking at over 90% for women under 30. For patients under 35, frozen blastocyst transfers yield a 65% to 80% clinical pregnancy rate per transfer. Even in complex scenarios—such as low AMH levels or recurrent implantation failures—cumulative success rates stay above 65%.

items.q: How much does IVF cost?
items.a: ₹1.5 lakh to ₹2.5 lakh for a complete cycle in most cases, with EMI options available.

items.q: Does age affect IVF success?
items.a: Yes. Success is highest under 35 and falls after 38 to 40 as egg quality declines, so early evaluation helps.

items.q: How many IVF cycles might I need?
items.a: Many couples conceive in 1 or 2 cycles; cumulative chances rise with each cycle, especially when spare embryos are frozen.

items.q: Can PCOS or endometriosis affect IVF?
items.a: Both can be managed well: OHSS-safe protocols for PCOS, and egg-sparing plans or surgery first for endometriosis.

items.q: Is sex selection allowed with IVF in India?
items.a: No. It is prohibited by the ART Act and the PC-PNDT Act and is never offered.

items.q: What are the age limits for IVF in India?
items.a: Under the ART (Regulation) Act, 2021, women must be 21 to 50 and men 21 to 55 when treatment starts.

items.q: Can I consult Dr. Dahiya online first?

items.q: Can single women have IVF in India?
items.a: Yes. Single women aged 21 to 50 can have treatment with their own eggs and donor sperm from a registered ART bank.

items.q: Does insurance cover IVF?
items.a: Standard plans usually do not; some corporate and women-centric policies do, with sub-limits and waiting periods.
